newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends slightly higher on corn, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends slightly higher on corn, weather.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures ended a shade higher on Tuesday on spillover from strength in corn and on continued concerns about weather problems in other wheat growing countries, traders said.
Corn posted modest gains on the day after the U.S. Agriculture Department's weekly crop update showed only a slight improvement in crop ratings despite last week's rain.

Wheat also drew strength from ongoing concerns about dry weather in Australia that was expected to leave this year's crop much smaller than last year's. There was also talk that India's crop would be smaller than expected.
Traders were eyeing the progress of monsoonal rains after some meteorologists warned that El Nino could lead to deficient rainfall amounts this year.
India was a major buyer of Australian wheat last year but drought-related losses there could force India to purchase U.S. wheat, traders said.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said Tuesday that India's monsoonal rains had picked up this week but noted that the crops needed four to six more weeks of rain.
Wheat ended 3-1/4 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher with December up three at $3.75-3/4.

The USDA weekly crop update also showed only minor improvements in the spring wheat crop. Harvest delays and reports of scab damage in that crop have kept MGE spring wheat futures firm and CBOT traders reported some spillover.

The export market was also heating up with Iraq buying 80,000 to 85,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat. Pakistan embassy officials said Tuesday that Pakistan would tender August 27 for 200,000 tonnes white wheat and there was persistent talk that Egypt would soon tender as well, traders said.
On the day, Cargill Inc and Continental Grain were light sellers of the December while Cargill Investor Services, FIMAT Futures and LFG each bought 0.5 million December.
In options, Smith Barney sold 400 September $3.60 calls at 3-1/2 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 12,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 13,789.
